project.title: Comprehensive N-glycoproteomic profiling of humanized antibody expressed in transgenic mouse serum
project.projectDescription: This dataset reports a comprehensive N-glycoproteomic profiling of serum-derived humanized antibodies expressed in transgenic mice using an intact glycopeptide (IGP)–based LC–MS/MS workflow. The study aimed to identify and characterize site-specific N-glycosylation modifications of mouse serum proteins, with emphasis on antibody-related glycoforms. Following sample digestion and HILIC enrichment, glycopeptides were analyzed by high-resolution Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometry in data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode. The identified N-linked glycopeptides were annotated for glycan composition, glycosylation heterogeneity, and functional classification through GO, KEGG, Reactome, and STRING analyses. The dataset provides an extensive resource for understanding host-dependent glycosylation patterns and their potential impact on antibody functionality.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Serum samples from transgenic mice were thawed on ice, centrifuged at 12,000 g for 10 min at 4°C to remove debris, and quantified using a BCA assay. Proteins were precipitated with cold acetone (1:5 v/v), washed twice, and resolubilized in 200 mM TEAB. Proteins were reduced with 5 mM DTT (56°C, 30 min), alkylated with 11 mM iodoacetamide (15 min, dark), and digested overnight with trypsin at a 1:50 (w/w) enzyme-to-substrate ratio. Resulting peptides were dissolved in 200 μL HILIC buffer (80% acetonitrile, 5% TFA) and loaded onto hydrophilic interaction microcolumns. After three washes, N-glycopeptides were eluted sequentially with 0.1% TFA, 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, and 50% acetonitrile. Desalted eluates were vacuum-dried and analyzed by LC–MS/MS. Chromatographic separation was performed using a Vanquish Neo UHPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer with a nano-ESI source. Mobile phases consisted of 0.1% formic acid in water (A) and 0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile (B). The gradient ranged from 4% to 99% B over 34 min at 400 nL/min.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw MS files were searched using MSFragger (v3.4) integrated in FragPipe (v20). Database searches were performed against the UniProt Mus musculus reference proteome supplemented with antibody sequences (XB03428.fasta, 17,194 entries) concatenated with reverse decoy sequences. Trypsin/P was specified as the digestion enzyme with up to 2 missed cleavages allowed. Precursor and fragment ion tolerances were set to 20 ppm. Fixed modification: carbamidomethyl (C); variable modifications: oxidation (M), acetylation (Protein N-term), and mass offsets for N-linked glycosylation. PSM- and protein-level FDRs were controlled at 1%. Identified intact glycopeptides were classified into five glycan types (paucimannose, high mannose, complex/hybrid, fucosylated, sialylated) following Riley et al., Nat Commun (2019). Downstream bioinformatics analyses, including GO, KEGG, Protein domain, Reactome, WikiPathways, and STRING (v12), were performed using R packages and Fisher’s exact test for enrichment. Protein–protein interaction networks were visualized via the R package visNetwork.
